title: Microtask Stack Handoff and Route Resume Playbook
content:
Summary:

This is a working playbook for implementing a compact, task-preserving microtask stack in the Console that lets users hop between related routes without losing context. Goal is to improve developer productivity for multi-step workflows (model testing -> evaluate -> deploy / rollout) and reduce task loss when navigation errors or network blips occur. This doc bundles UX notes, wireframe writeups, and a prioritized backlog for an MVP and two follow-up phases.

Problem we see:
- Users traversing the Console frequently juggle multiple related pages (prompt playground, model settings, rollout config, logs). Currently deep-links are brittle: a back button or a direct link can lose in-memory state (unsaved prompt values, local filters, ephemeral KV caches).
- Task flow is linear: switching to another area forces a full reset, causing rework and frustration (we see support tickets and NPS comments).
- Mobile and narrow-window UX crushes the sidebar; users rely on breadcrumbs which don't capture transient task state.

Principles:
- Task-first navigation: surface the active task stack at the top-left as a compact strip (microtask strip) rather than forcing the sidebar to be authoritative for transient state.
- Non-destructive routing: route changes should preserve an ordered microtask stack per workspace and allow resume by click or deep-link.
- Predictable URLs: every stack entry corresponds to a stable URL (with tokenized resume state when necessary) to allow copy/paste, bookmarking, and cross-tab resume.
- Graceful degradation: if external state cannot be restored (expired cache, removed model), reveal a recovery UI instead of a 404.

Wireframe notes (sketch-level):
- Microtask strip (compact horizontal pill bar) sits below top nav and above page content. Each pill shows: icon, short title (max 22 chars), chevron for quick-preview. Active pill is highlighted. Pills are reorderable via drag.
- Pill click behaviour: primary click navigates to saved route + 'resume token' applied; secondary click (chevron) opens a small preview card anchored to pill with last-saved params and quick actions (save snapshot, close, duplicate, open in new tab).
- URL design: /org/:orgId/workspace/:wsId/stack/:stackId/entry/:entryId?resume=hash. Resume hash encodes ephemeral params (base64 JSON) but expires after 30 days for hygiene. For long-lived snapshots we create a named snapshot resource.
- Fallbacks: if resume token invalid -> show 'Resume failed' overlay with actions: recreate from last known, open clean route, or report bug.

MVP scope (Q2 sprint):
- Implement microtask strip component with in-memory stack per workspace.
- Persist stack metadata (titles, route paths, small metadata) in localStorage and sync to the new 'stack-snapshots' microservice (backend work limited to metadata only).
- Create URL pattern that references a stack entry by id and supports resume tokens.
- Preserve playground prompt contents and page-level filters for resume (first-class fields).
- Quick-preview (chevron) opens a lightweight overlay (no heavy reconnections).
- Add telemetry: RESUME_CLICK, RESUME_FAIL, STACK_PUSH, STACK_POP, STACK_REORDER.

Backlog (prioritized):
1) UX polish for pill truncation rules and overflow menu (must support keyboard shortcuts).
2) Named snapshots (user can save a stack state to DB with description).
3) Cross-tab sync and conflict resolution.
4) Native mobile adaptation: transform strip into vertically collapsible toast anchored to top of content.
5) Integration with rollouts and canary controls so a 'deploy' stack entry shows live health.
6) RBAC: ensure stacks and snapshots respect org/team permissions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can open/close/restore a stack entry and be back on the same page with prompt values and filters restored 90% of the time in automated tests.
- URL resume tokens restore state when opened in a new tab within 24 hours.
- RESUME_FAIL rate < 5% in staging (measured by telemetry) before ship.

Technical constraints and notes:
- We cannot store full request bodies or secrets in resume tokens. Mask any api_key-like fields; recommend storing opaque references for credentials.
- Resume token size should be under 2KB. If bigger, use server snapshot reference.
- For private deployments (VPC), snapshot API must respect no-telemetry policy; default to local-only unless the admin enables snapshot service.
- Cache keys: route + workspace + stackId. KV cache eviction policy for snapshots: LRU with 90-day TTL for named snapshots, 30-day for ephemeral tokens.

Telemetry and success metrics (proposal):
- Adoption: percent of active users with >1 stack entry created per week. Target 25% in month 1 post-launch.
- Recovery rate: percent of resume attempts that fully restored state. Target 95% for basic fields.
- Task completion delta: compare conversion (deploy success) for flows that used stacks vs those that didn't (expect +8–12%).
- Support tickets: reduce console-navigation-related tickets by 20% within quarter.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (internal): feature flag behind "microtask-stack-alpha" for selected eng/product users. Duration 2 weeks. Gather qualitative notes.
- Beta: open to all orgs with opt-in toggle. Telemetry gating: resume_fail < 8% and adoption > 10% over 2 weeks.
- Gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with kill-switch if RESUME_FAIL spikes > 15%.

A/B experiment ideas:
- Show microtask pills vs persistent sidebar mini-mode for new users. Metric: task completion time for multi-step flows.
- Default to named snapshots vs ephemeral tokens for enterprise orgs; measure snapshot creation frequency and storage cost.

Edge cases and open questions (workshop items):
- How to represent ephemeral vs named stacks in the UI to avoid clutter? (UX hypothesis: collapse ephemeral under 'Recent' and highlight pinned named stacks).
- Should non-owner collaborators see the same stack or get a shadow copy? (security implications).
- Conflicting edits: two users toggle the same rollout config from same stack; need conflict UX.
- How do we limit the amount of detail encoded in resume tokens for larger editors (e.g., long prompt histories)? Strategy: only capture last N steps with heuristics.

Design sketches (textual):
- Top nav (left to right): logo | org selector | workspace name | microtask strip (pills) | primary actions (new item) | account menu.
- Pill: [ModelIcon] "Playground: gpt-xt"  › (chevron). Hover shows preview card: small header with timestamp, bullet list of preserved fields, actions icons (snapshot, open, close).
- Overflow menu on strip: shows chronological list + 'Restore All' and 'Clear Recent'.

Developer notes (implementation checklist):
- Frontend: component in console/ui/packages/microtask-strip; keyboard-focusable, aria-labels for a11y.
- Backend: stack-snapshots service (metadata-only endpoint): POST /v1/snapshots, GET /v1/snapshots/:id, DELETE. Auth: scoped keys.
- SDK: add resume token helper in console-sdk to encode/decode and validate TTL.
- Tests: unit tests for pill ARIA attributes, integration tests for URL-based restore, e2e for cross-tab sync.

Communication and docs:
- Draft a short how-to in Console help: "Resume tasks and snapshots" with GIF.
- Add product note in changelog + feature flag rollout announcement in #product-release.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Sync with Ravi (frontend lead) to finalize pill accessibility behaviors. (Action: Ravi to propose keyboard mapping by Thu).
- Morgan to prototype preview card HTML/CSS and share in Figma.
- Sofia to write initial telemetry plan and p95 targets for RESUME latency.
- Create JIRA epic CON-842 and link to this doc.

Notes to self / TODO fragments:
- remind: consider storage implications for enterprise customers with many named snapshots.
- prototype tiny animation for pill insertion to help scan.
- check Privacy team guidance on short-lived tokens and base64 encoding.

References and inspirations:
- Gmail "tasks" top strip concept (not identical, but behavior inspiration).
- VSCode "restore editor sessions" behavior for cross-tab restore.
- Prior Console bug thread: slack thread #console-navigation -> thread ts 1683321100.

End of playbook (working draft). Comments inline welcome — tag @alyssa for major changes.
